minimumMeaningfulDifference.statement: Recall is averaged over 60 queries, so one query flipping moves mean recall by at most 1/60 = 0.0167. Only a gap of 3 or more queries (>=5.0 pts) is interpretable. q-051..q-060 were added after the original 50; the v1 subset stays comparable to earlier runs, the full set does not.
minimumMeaningfulDifference.notes: relevantAtomIds are author judgements made by reading the atom bodies, never by running a retriever. They are believed sufficient, not provably exhaustive: an unlisted atom that also answers a query depresses measured precision equally for every adapter, so cross-adapter comparison stays valid while absolute precision is a lower bound. Queries q-051..q-055 (document disambiguation) and q-056..q-058 (aggregation) were selected by SECTION HEADING from the source document, never from retriever output, to keep the judgement independent of the system under test. They reuse the existing closed axis vocabulary (multi-word-phrase / production-shaped-long-form) because adding an axis would require a schema change.

queries.query: I need to change the agentic code runner because a task keeps failing at the tsc stage. Before I touch anything I want to know where the change belongs: the task DAG builder, the speckit orchestrator, or the runner harness itself. The symptom is that the model does not seem to have enough information about the collaborator modules it must call, and separately the test gate reported a failure when the test tool itself crashed and produced no summary line at all. I want to understand the rule about which component owns which defect, the rule about not encoding tool-specific flags or output grammar into harness code, and what questions I am supposed to answer before editing at all - what this buys, by which measured metric, whether I am fixing the root cause or a symptom, whether the change is visible to the model, and whether something could be removed instead of added. I also want the statement of the overall goal the harness serves, so I can check that a change that improves a benchmark is not in fact violating the vision. Please give me the ownership boundaries, the gate-tool contract, the pre-edit checklist, the minimalism rule about new knobs and config fields, and the goal statement about quality, proven, minimal.
queries.rationale: Production shape: several hundred words assembled from a task target plus symptom detail. Each named sub-question maps to exactly one atom - ownership boundaries table, gate-tool contract (no tool burn-in, fail fast), ROI gate questions, minimalism (a new knob is a last resort), and the goals/vision statement.

queries.query: Task: refactor an oversized container in a React feature so it passes the project gates. The container currently sits at about 140 lines, keeps a boolean for whether a confirm dialog is open, keeps a submitting flag while an async save runs, holds a per-row editing flag for a list, and computes a filtered and sorted array inline inside the JSX return. It also has two useEffect calls: one that calls a store load action on mount and one that reacts to a prop change by calling setState. I need to know the hard line limit for a container and what to do when it is exceeded, which pieces of local useState are permitted and which must move into the store, how the store selectors must be written so a Zustand v5 subscription does not re-render forever, which useEffect cases survive and what tag comment each one requires on the line immediately above it, and the rule that forbids logic and anonymous functions inside the JSX template. Give me the role table for renderer, container and page as well, because part of the fix is pushing the JSX down into a renderer that receives everything through props.
queries.rationale: Production shape: a task statement plus concrete code facts. Sub-questions map to the roles table (80-line ceiling, props-only renderers), the four-tag useEffect policy, the Zustand v5 selector-stability table, the local-UI-state allowlist (dialog flags, loading flags, editingId belong in the store), and the two logicless-template atoms.

queries.query: I am writing a new Playwright end-to-end spec for a settings flow that configures a provider, sends a message and verifies the reply persists across a page reload. I must not call a live model. I need the fixture that parametrizes the spec per locale and provides the translation function and the regex bag, the rule that forbids hardcoded user-facing text literals in assertions, the stub installer for the LLM endpoints and the requirement to re-install those route handlers after a reload, the locator policy that says which of testid, role-with-accessible-name and text assertion to use where, and the total spec budget for the repository, because if the suite is already at the ceiling I have to merge or remove a spec rather than add one. Also tell me the expected shape of a spec: how many steps, how the step names are written, and whether a spec may depend on another spec having run first.
queries.rationale: Production shape: a spec-authoring brief. Each clause maps to one E2E standards atom - forEachLocale, the t(key) rule, installLlmStubs, the reload re-install pattern, the 3-tier locator policy, the 40-spec cap, the 5-20 step flow style, and the independence rule.

queries.query: A phase needs a new npm package that ships a multi-megabyte WASM asset and bundled model weights. Before I install anything I have to follow the project protocol. I need the sequence: exhaust native and existing alternatives first, then the research step and who performs it, then the architecture decision record that must be written and where it goes, then the explicit user approval wording, then the install step and what else must be updated. On top of that, because this dependency ships heavy binary assets, there is an extra gate that must run at the end of the phase that installs it rather than being deferred to pre-merge: a build plus a precache size assertion, with a documented per-asset limit and a named fix in the vite config when an asset exceeds it. I also want the precedent for how such a dependency was admitted before, including the constraints that it must be loaded through a lazy dynamic import inside a flag-gated path only, that model weights go to cache storage on demand, and that a one-time download consent prompt is persisted.
queries.rationale: Production shape: a governance brief. The five numbered steps map one-to-one to the five step atoms; the heavy-asset paragraph maps to the WASM gate atom; the precedent paragraph maps to the ADR-024 Decision (lazy import, cache storage, consent, flag gate) and the ADR-033 five-step Decision.

queries.query: A runner run reports status completed and the summary says the red-then-green transition was observed, but when I look at the final working tree the implementation is there and I cannot find any test that verifies it. The run also recorded a nonzero reset count. Separately, two earlier attempts in the same run failed at the same stage with byte-identical gate output while the model was clearly editing files, and there were no guard rejections at all. I want the diagnosis method for a reported success whose evidence no longer exists - the status fields that must be read together rather than status alone, how to count the feature identifiers across the per-attempt snapshots, and which pipeline shape makes greenObserved degrade into merely nothing failed. I also want the method that distinguishes a walled-off model from a weak one by intersecting the files the gate errored on with the files the drive actually wrote, and the method for work that regresses between attempts through the replan and reset layer. Finally give me the known false positives that have burned prior sessions on exactly these signals.
queries.rationale: Production shape: a diagnosis brief with three interleaved symptoms. They map to method 8 (status provenance / false green), method 9 (drive-scope vs gate-scope), method 7 (state continuity / reset poisoning), the known-traps atom that covers greenObserved on gate-only pipelines and collapsed co-located test snapshots, and the triage symptom table that routes all three.

queries.query: I am planning where a new concept belongs in the codebase. It persists a new kind of record, it has its own page in the UI, and two existing features will both need its value-object type. I do not want to guess. I need the mechanical decision tree that is followed from the top - does it persist data, is it a new entity type, does it have its own significant surface, does it pass the removal test, does it wrap an external protocol, is it shared across two or more features, is it stateless types and constants, is it pure logic - together with the rule that the tree is run once per concern rather than once per feature, because this concept clearly decomposes into a persistence file, a feature module and a shared type. I also need the thresholds that say when a feature directory, a domain module, a service file, a service module and a utility file are each justified, the per-directory import table saying what each layer may and may not import, the statement that imports flow downward and that cross-feature access goes through the barrel, and the removal test itself.
queries.rationale: Production shape: a placement brief spanning three source documents. The Q1..Q9 tree, the decomposition rule and the how-to-use steps come from the placement tree; the create-when thresholds from layer boundaries; the per-directory table and the downward-direction diagram from module dependency rules; the barrel rule from ADR-030; and the removal test from the responsibility rules.
